proposed_comments.title: Make profile-resource integration tests hermetic

confidence.rationale: The current test class directly uses SettingsUtils.Default and the production Keyboard Manager reload event; cleanup restores disk files but does not reload the restored state in a running engine.

proposed_comments.body:
### Make profile-resource integration tests hermetic

**Severity:** `high`

These tests still replace the signed-in user's real Keyboard Manager `settings.json`, `default.json`, and `work.json` files and signal the production reload event. A running Keyboard Manager instance can therefore load the temporary sample profile, and cleanup restores the files without signaling another reload, so the test mappings may remain active until the engine restarts. Please inject isolated settings storage and a test-only signaling dependency (including the elevation check) so the suite never reads, writes, or signals live user state.

testInstructions: Launch the already-built runner at <PowerToysCheckout>\x64\Debug\PowerToys.exe and enable Keyboard Manager.
From a non-elevated shell, run <PowerToysCheckout>\x64\Debug\PowerToys.DSC.exe export --resource profile --module KeyboardManager and save the current output.
Apply a disposable profile with set, confirm the remapping activates without restarting PowerToys, then use test to verify the desired state.
Restore the exported profile and verify key, shortcut, chord, app-specific, text, run-program, URI, and tap-alone condition entries round-trip without loss.
